tag: Episode 24 · Because There Is No Water
title: Because There Is No Water

beats.t: At dawn, mist lay low along the river. A pink pig slept curled on a wet stone.
A white hair was wound around one hoof. Refastened who knew how many times through the night, the knot had three layers.
Found you. You really slept here?
Moka. Where's Yeongnyangi?
Not yet.
Yeoni nodded. They did not cry. Their face had cried all it could through the night, with nothing left to give.
My lady, let's go inside first. Sleep on cold stones, and Eul Wood takes damage from the roots up.
What would I do inside? If I stay here, I'll see him as soon as he comes back.
Go inside and eat. If the cat comes back and sees you like this, he'll get mad at me. I don't want that.
Moka took Yeoni's scruff in his teeth and dragged them. Even as they were pulled away, Yeoni kept looking back at the river.
Mist over the water scattered and gathered again. Between it, one black ripple passed silently. Nobody saw.
Unfamiliar objects stood on the long reading-room table. A kettle, a metal spoon, a plant pot, and a candle.
All right, class begins. Today's tuition is your birth date and time, my lady.
You already know it.
Some things you want to hear again even when you know them.
Con artist, is this really the time?
It is. There's no cheaper way to put a smile on our lady's face.
Yeoni did not smile. But they raised their head a little. As though that were enough, Yundal picked up the metal spoon.
This is Mr. Cat. Gyeong Metal. Hard, sharp, able to cut Wood.
Yundal tapped the small tree in the pot with the spoon's tip. One leaf fell.
Don't.
Yes. That's why Mr. Cat was always careful beside you. Metal controls Wood—金克木. Metal overcomes Wood.
Then we were wrong for each other from the start. Yeongnyangi and me.
No. This is where the real lesson begins.
Yundal lifted the kettle and poured water over the spoon. The water ran along it and soaked into the pot's soil.
Metal generates Water. Water nourishes Wood. With Water between them, Metal feeds Wood instead of cutting it.
[ 庚 Influence → 壬 Resource → 乙 Day Master · Officer and Resource in Mutual Generation ]
It's called Officer and Resource in Mutual Generation. Officer generates Resource, and Resource generates me. A way for Mr. Cat to become a well instead of a blade.
The little tree drank and spread its leaves slightly. Yeoni stared at those leaves for a long time.
Then... Yeongnyangi doesn't have to hurt?
As long as there's Water.
And the fire? You said the pig's fire melts the cat.
Water for that, too.
Yundal lightly cupped his palm above the candle. Its flame did not go out. It merely stopped wavering and shrank to a suitable size.
Resource guides Hurting Officer. Hurting Officer Balanced by Resource. Not putting out the fire, but giving it a path.
(I don't have to put it out. Even if I don't, Yeongnyangi won't get hurt.)
For the first time, light returned to Yeoni's eyes. Bracing against the table, they sprang up.
Water. All we need is water. Where is it? There's a whole river full!
Probably not that water.
Why?!
If it were that water, I'd have dunked the cat in the river already.
Mr. Otter is right. River water is just water. We need the Water in your chart.
Your Year Stem. Im Water, 壬. That's your Resource.
The three went down to the memory vault. Yeoni's chart floated at its center. Seven of its eight slots were lit.
[ Year 壬午 · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  7/8
The first character, 壬, looked more like a lump of ice than writing. Frozen black, it held something writhing inside.
Why is it like this? It's been this way since we found it in the library.
Because you recovered it from the tiger. That tiger's water is cold and black. It froze yours.
That striped jerk. Every time we see it, it breaks something else before leaving.
Then we melt it.
My lady, wait.
Yeoni had already raised a hoof. An ember of Byeong Fire formed at its tip.
You melt ice with fire. I've got plenty of fire.
That's the problem!
Flames wrapped around 壬. White steam rose from the ice. Then pain split the inside of Yeoni's chest as though it were cracking apart.
Ah—it hurts!
Yeoni did not withdraw the fire. Gritting their teeth, they pushed their hoof farther forward. One fine crack appeared in the ice.
Through it, another scene poured in. Rain was falling. Water streamed in strings from the edge of a bus stop roof.
Someone stood alone in a corner of the stop. Without an umbrella. Wet hair covered their face, hiding it.
An umbrella tilted halfway toward that person. The hand holding it was small and familiar. Yeoni's own hand.
Laughter sounded beyond the rain. Yeoni couldn't tell whose. Warm laughter, a little shy.
The scene broke. Yeoni lost hold of the fire. Where the steam settled, 壬 remained frozen. If anything, the crack had turned darker.
What was that? A bus stop. Rain. I've never been there.
A memory trapped inside the ice. Yours, yet one you don't know.
Pig, your nose is bleeding.
Yeoni rubbed their nose. Red stained their hoof. Their chest still throbbed inside.
Melt this ice with fire, and the water boils away. It all burns off before the thawed water can nourish you.
Then how do I melt it? What do I have besides fire?
I don't know yet, either. Ice is usually easiest to release when the one who froze it does the thawing.
That tiger would never do that for us.
Exactly.
The vault fell quiet. Inside the frozen 壬, the smell of rain lingered very faintly.
By afternoon, Yeoni could no longer sit still. Pacing around the reading room, they bumped into the table's corner three times.
Let's split up and search. For Yeongnyangi and for Water. I'll go crazy just sitting here.
All right. I'll take the lower shelves. Plenty of books about Water there.
I'll try the market. Ask if a cat-shaped thing passed by. White, round, grumpy. Wearing a hat.
I'll take the river. That's where I last saw him.
My lady. Let's meet here again before sunset. The sky's strange today.
Yundal pointed outside. Yesterday's cracked sky was strangely dark today. A corner of the sun looked as though something had bitten into it.
What's wrong with the sun? Just like on the festival island.
That's why I'm saying this. Don't stay alone too long.
At the same time, downstream, a white cat sat where the mist was thickest.
Yeongnyangi soaked his rusted paw in the river. Where the water touched it, tiny amounts of rust loosened and flowed away. Very tiny amounts.
Metal generates Water. With Water, I don't have to be a blade.
The same words Yundal had spoken that morning. No one had taught them to Yeongnyangi. He simply knew.
That child's Water is still frozen. As Metal, I can't melt it myself.
Yeongnyangi looked at his reflection in the river. His violet eyes briefly rippled gold, then settled again.
You told me to step aside.
He murmured it once more, as though turning the words over in his mouth. Then he smiled very faintly.
Still, your fire was there. That's a relief.
The river turned black. Dozens of black hands shot from the water at once, exactly where Yeongnyangi's paw had been soaking.
Did you miss Water, cat? Here it is. Closest to you when you are weakest.
You. The one who cracked the sky above the library.
You made that crack. To stay beside that child, you thrust a blade into someone else's chart.
Yeongnyangi stood. A golden blade rose from his rusted paw. But it was half as long as yesterday, with rust spreading along its tip.
The blade severed three black hands. They came back as six. Six became twelve.
You are a borrowed slot. What's borrowed must be returned. Leave that child, and sink into me.
No. That child is my only assignment.
One black hand seized Yeongnyangi's scruff. Another his left paw, another his tail. His small body was dragged toward the water.
Yeoni.
Halfway through calling the name, Yeongnyangi closed his mouth. If he called, Yeoni would come. And then that child would stand before these hands.
Without another sound, the white cat was dragged into black water. One great ripple rose, then the river grew impossibly calm.
Nothing remained on the bank. Mist settled again.
At sunset, Moka turned toward the river on his way back from the market. Because of something he'd heard there: a white, round thing had gone downstream.
Cat? Hey, Customer Support. Answer if you're there. I came to tell on the pig for crying all night.
No answer. Sniffing, Moka stepped from wet stone to wet stone. The smell of melting metal mingled with an unfamiliar cold scent.
A large palmprint marked the mud beside the water. Much larger than a human hand, its fingers far too long. At its center lay a strand of white fur.
This.
Moka picked it up. Yeongnyangi's fur. Just like the strand Yeoni wore around their hoof. But this one was cold. Colder than the river.
Moka! You came here, too? I went all the way downstream, but nothing...
Yeoni stopped. They saw the white fur in Moka's paw. And the great handprint in the mud beneath it.
Where did you get that?
Pig. Sit down. Sit down first and listen.
Where did you get it?!
Yundal ran up, panting. With his glove off, the hole in his palm swirled on its own, as though something enormous had just passed nearby.
We're late. Those hands were here just now. A great many of them.
[ Hour Stem 庚 · Borrowed slot · Connection lost ]
Inside Yeoni's chest, something snapped. Nobody else heard it. Only Yeoni.
They took Yeongnyangi.
The sun's last corner was eaten away. A black disk hung over the river. Red light burned in a ring around its rim.
The sun. The sun's gone.
An eclipse. It's finally revealing its body.
The cat arrived safely, little pig. My sheath was empty, so I had just the use for him.
Give him back. Give Yeongnyangi back!
I will. In return, you must come. As an empty vessel.
The black disk slowly blinked, like an eyelid. And every shadow over the river turned toward Yeoni.
